---
title: Methods and data
---

## Quantities

| Quantity | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Strength | Estimated ability at a specified date and reference context |
| Contribution | Value assigned to performances in completed matches |
| Runs above replacement | Run value relative to an explicitly defined substitute |
| WAR | Expected wins above that replacement baseline |
| Win probability added | Change in modeled winning probability around observed events |

These quantities answer different questions. Each model will keep its own scale,
uncertainty method, and assumptions. An estimate of zero relative to the average
player does not establish replacement level.

## Data and coverage

The source is [Cricsheet](https://cricsheet.org/downloads/), whose
[JSON documentation](https://cricsheet.org/format/json/) defines participants,
registries, replacements, and outcomes. Source data remain subject to
[Cricsheet's licensing terms](https://cricsheet.org/licensing/).

The implemented preparation stage supports official JSON and the existing YAML
downloads. It writes separate Test, ODI, and T20I match and participant tables, plus player
identity tables. Delivery records remain in the raw source for subsequent ball-level work.
The source receipt and per-file hashes identify the exact input snapshot.

Coverage is the set of available source matches, not a certified census of international
cricket. Men's and women's source coverage may differ. The manifest reports counts
separately and distinguishes exclusions after the requested cutoff from other
formats. It does not infer that a complete historical archive was available at
an earlier forecast date.

## Participants and eligibility

Cricsheet's `players` lists include replacements as well as the starting eleven.
The participant table therefore makes no starting-XI claim. A match is flagged
`has_fixed_xi=1` only if each side lists eleven distinct people and no match
replacement or supersub is recorded. The initial binary lineup eligibility flag
additionally requires a decisive result. The Test ranking model also admits fixed-XI draws and ties. These are sample
flags, not deletions.

Stable IDs are required for every listed participant. Missing IDs, duplicated
participants, invalid outcomes, and duplicate match IDs stop preparation with the
source filename. Missing participant lists remain visible as ineligible matches.
Names are preserved per appearance; the identity table uses each person's latest
observed name within the cutoff. Team labels and venue labels remain source
strings, so joins to external team ratings need an audited mapping.

Ties, draws, and no-results remain distinct. A tie resolved by an eliminator is
retained as a tie with the eliminator recorded separately. Toss and outcome fields
are separate: outcome-dependent information must not enter pre-match predictions.

## Selection and match difficulty

A player who appears mainly in easier fixtures can receive an inflated rating if
the model misses what makes those fixtures easy. The current model includes all
22 player identities: weaker opposing XIs and stronger teammates therefore enter
the predictor, alongside the toss and batting first. This adjusts for some
schedule differences, following the logic of
[regularized adjusted plus-minus](https://faculty.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/shanejensen.pmlogit.2013.pdf).
It does not make team selection random.

The present ratings do **not** separately adjust for home advantage, neutral
venues, pitch suitability, injuries, player availability, or changes in underlying
team conditions over the five-year window. A specialist selected only on favorable
pitches, or a reserve selected only against weaker touring sides, can remain
confounded with those conditions. Shrinkage addresses instability; it does not
remove this selection bias.

The next comparison should add audited home/away/neutral status and venue context,
and examine team strength measured strictly before each match. A team-strength
baseline changes the target: player coefficients then describe departures from
that baseline. It should be reported as a separate specification, with changes in
rankings and chronological predictive performance, rather than treated as an
automatic correction to the existing player-only rankings.

A useful diagnostic is each player's distribution of pre-match fixture difficulty
and whether alternative players actually appear in comparable fixtures. Little
overlap means estimates depend heavily on extrapolation. Selection weighting would
require a defensible pool of available but unselected players and measured selection
predictors; playing XIs alone do not provide that information. Such adjustment
still relies on no important unmeasured confounding and adequate overlap. See
[Goetghebeur et al. on causal questions and adjustment](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8741).

Use pre-match conditions for these comparisons. Final run margins, wickets, and
match performances are consequences of the lineup and must not be added as
controls for its pre-match contribution. The published rankings remain descriptive
model associations, with selection bias unresolved.

## Existing WAR calculations

The original notebooks used an assumed runs-to-wins divisor and a percentile or
scaled-expectation replacement baseline. Mean victory margin among matches won
by runs is not a marginal runs-per-win estimate. The original calculations are
preserved for inspection, with their limitations, in
[the exploratory collection](https://github.com/outside-edge/player_value/tree/main/experiments).
